cues.say: Component 8: Conditional update. Check and change in one database command: subtract 1 only if at least 1 is left. The database runs it as a single step. You'll bring this up during version one and the spike, to protect what must never break.
Think of it as: Grabbing the last item off a shelf: only one hand can take it. Use it for no oversell, stock, seats, and time slots.
Here's a real scenario. 1 TV left on sale. Alice and Bob click Buy in the same millisecond.
Without it: Both read left equals 1.
With it: both run this one statement. It subtracts one only where at least one is left.
Bob: 0 rows changed, sees sold out.
Why it works: The database refuses to go below zero, no matter how close the clicks.
In the interview, say: One statement, so the database refuses to go below zero.
A few related terms you may hear.
SELECT ... FOR UPDATE: Lock the row for complex logic; others wait.
Redis counter: Avoid: then two places hold the truth.
Distributed lock: Avoid: the database already does this.
